sentences.text: Zalmoxes was a small, bipedal herbivore characterized by a large triangular head and a beak.
This extinct genus includes two known species of ornithopod dinosaurs belonging to the subfamily Rhabdodontinae and the class Ornithischia, which is part of the parent group Rhabdodontoidea.
The genus name honors the Dacian deity Zalmoxis, while the species name Z. shqiperorum refers to the Albanian people.

Adult Z. robustus reached up to 2.5 meters in length and 45 kilograms in body mass, whereas subadults of this species measured between 2 and 2.4 meters, and the larger species Z. shqiperorum is known from a subadult individual measuring 2.5 meters.
Ossified tendons were found in the juvenile specimen of Z. shqiperorum, showing they were circular or elliptical in cross-section with fine striations.
The genus was first named in 1899 by Franz Nopcsa as the species Mochlodon robustum, but it was reclassified as Zalmoxes robustus in 2003.
Numerous fossils found in Transylvania were initially identified by Baron Franz Nopcsa during his early work on the region.
A new species, Zalmoxes shqiperorum, was identified in 2003 based on new remains found in Romania.
Zalmoxes was a more robust animal than its precursors and advanced relatives, possessing a very strong morphology.
Studies suggested Zalmoxes ate tough fibrous plants including soft shoots, horsetails, angiosperms, pteridophytes, and ferns, and could process and digest C3 plants.

Nopcsa proposed that Zalmoxes adapted through insular dwarfism because it was smaller than its relatives in the Hateg Basin, though later research by Osi and colleagues found the size similar to that of rhabdodontid ancestors.

In 2003, Weishampel et al. established the family Rhabdodontidae for Mochlodon, Rhabdodon, and Zalmoxes, classifying it as a derived group within Iguanodontia and placing them phylogenetically between Talenkauen and Tenontosaurus.
Fossils are found in the Sânpetru, Sebes, and Densuş-Ciula Formations in the Hateg Island region of Romania.
It is debated whether Zalmoxes shqiperorum is an ornithopod or a ceratopsian, with recent studies in 2026 placing it in Ceratopsia.
